content.text: You're a [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-broken-here|COREMERCH guide to digital]] creator in a region where [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/stripe-alternatives-nigerian-creators-honest-side-side-breakdown-7|stripe]], PayPal, and other conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators-works-how|How Payment]] processors are blocked or severely restricted. This leaves you with no choice but to rely on sketchy workarounds or abandon your online store altogether. In this post, we'll show you how to build a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, a platform that's free from the clutches of these restrictive payment processors. We'll explore the infrastructure behind Stack 01 and Stack 02, and walk you through the process of setting up your own crypto store from scratch.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The reason why this infrastructure works when platforms fail is that it's built on open-source technologies that are free from the restrictions imposed by Stripe, PayPal, and other conventional payment processors. By hosting your store on Cloudflare Pages, you're leveraging a platform that's designed to be flexible and scalable, allowing you to accept payments from customers all over the world without worrying about platform restrictions.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can deploy your crypto store, you'll need to set up a few essential components. First, you'll need to create a GitHub Pages site or a Cloudflare Pages site, depending on the infrastructure stack you choose. Next, you'll need to configure your payment and delivery pipeline using NOWPayments and Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. Finally, you'll need to set up your product catalog and configure your store's settings.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to integrate NOWPayments with Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. This will allow you to accept on-chain crypto payments from your customers and automatically deliver your products to them. You'll also need to configure your store's settings to ensure that payments are processed correctly and that products are delivered promptly.
With Stack 02, you can build a robust and scalable infrastructure for your crypto store that meets the demands of your growing customer base.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto. Fourth: check your order database and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.
